A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BBFlow and retain matching methodological and experimental content. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including identification of moved and removed material.

before.justification: V1 reports original BBFlow training and evaluation, simulations of de novo proteins, feature ablations, and a timestep study.

after.justification: V2 reports original evaluations on ATLAS, de novo proteins, and multi-chain systems, alongside robustness experiments, ablations, and BBFlow-light results.

M1.justification: V1 uses absolute/relative residue-position encodings and excludes directional features from default BBFlow. V2 removes index encodings and incorporates directional features for residues within 5 Å. Appendix A.6 also introduces BBFlow-light with three rather than six CFA blocks and smaller feature dimensions. The conditional-prior construction and training loss remain.

E1.justification: ATLAS and the de novo dataset are retained. V2 adds evaluation on five multi-chain systems despite monomer-only training, substantially extending the represented protein population. Appendix A.1 also tests AlphaFold2-predicted, noise-perturbed, and randomly selected MD conformations as input structures.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated comparisons with BioEmu on ATLAS and de novo proteins, and MDGen, Str2Str, and ESMDiff on ATLAS (Tables 1–2 and A.3). It also tests a modified AlphaFlow parser on a multi-chain complex. The original comparator set is retained; NMA and MSA subsampling remain literature-based comparisons rather than newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds DCCM and Ramachandran-distribution evaluation, input-structure perturbation protocols, training/inference sweeps of the prior parameter, and dataset-averaged speed–accuracy comparisons. Reported inference hardware changes from A100-40GB to A100-80GB. The ATLAS split, 250 generated conformations per protein, training budget, and default 20 timesteps remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 revises the feature-ablation comparison and adds initial-structure sensitivity, prior-parameter sensitivity, backbone-dihedral analysis, ensemble case studies, and backbone-versus-sidechain runtime analysis. Conversely, v1's timestep sweep (Table A.2) and per-protein PCA plots (Figure A.3) are absent from v2, rather than merely relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions estimate finite-sampling errors using 100 bootstraps of MD conformations and display errors above the reported precision. V2 adds no distinct seed-reporting, repeated-training-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure; its checklist reiterates the existing practice.

E6.justification: Results expand substantially through new baselines, multi-chain tests, robustness studies, and BBFlow-light. For revised BBFlow, ATLAS RMSF MAE changes from 0.47 to 0.42 Å, while de novo RMSF MAE changes from 0.23 to 0.26 Å (Tables 1–2). ATLAS transient-contact J changes from 0.35 to 0.29 (v1 Table A.1; v2 Table A.9). These are mixed results for revised configurations, not a uniform same-setting gain.

T1.justification: The flow equations, geodesic conditional prior, and loss retain their mathematical substance; the prior parameter is renamed from δt to ξ. Added training pseudocode and the standard DCCM formula explain procedures and metrics. Removing the FAPE background exposition does not change the underlying theory, and neither version introduces proofs or theoretical results.

C1.justification: V2 adds a central claim of transfer from monomers to multi-chain proteins, including claimed first applicability among ensemble-generation models. It also narrows the introduction and conclusion toward standardized MD emulation, explicitly qualifying the evolutionary-information claim by ensembles observed during 300 ns of MD. The original efficiency and structure-conditioning contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly limits applicability to MD-derived distributions, discusses inaccessible distant folding states, weaker transient-contact prediction, and absent sidechain and ligand modeling. It connects index removal to multimer transfer and adds caveats about ensemble metrics and differently trained baselines. Directional encoding is now interpreted as beneficial within the revised model, whereas v1 emphasized its over-stabilization.

D1.justification: V2 adds training pseudocode, model parameter counts, BBFlow-light dimensions, multimer identities, and detailed AlphaFlow multimer-input preparation. V1 only promises release of code, weights, and data; v2 supplies a BBFlow repository address and states availability, although its checklist retains future-tense release wording. Existing de novo simulation and ConfDiff setup details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes positioning around standardized MD emulation versus broader ensemble generation. It adds discussion and citations for MDGen, Str2Str, ESMDiff, accelerated AlphaFlow, dynamics-aware design, and applications of short-timescale MD. It also introduces multimer novelty positioning and explicitly qualifies comparisons with models trained on different ensemble distributions.

P1.justification: Related work is reorganized into distinct ensemble-generation categories, the AlphaFlow/FAPE background is condensed, and detailed metric exposition moves from the main text to Appendix A.3. The discussion and conclusion are rewritten around MD emulation and limitations, while the appendix is extensively reorganized and a conference checklist is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two-column to single-column layout. V1 Figures 3–4 are combined into v2 Figure 2, and the prior illustration moves to Appendix Figure A.4. Tables gain different metric columns, and new ensemble, DCCM, dihedral, and speed–accuracy displays accompany removal of the PCA montage and timestep table.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation through input-structure robustness tests, local-geometry checks, broader comparisons, and demonstrated multimer transfer. Its explicit restriction to short MD-derived distributions and discussion of transient-contact weaknesses address important gaps in v1's applicability claims. Some scores worsen and the timestep/PCA diagnostics disappear, but the stronger supporting evidence and clearer limitations provide a substantial net improvement in paper quality.
